facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s presented with a 2-year history of multiple asymptomatic lesions on the face and neck
The lesions were round, hypopigmented macules and were symmetrically distributed in the affected area
The macules had appeared on his cheeks 2 years earlier and had gradually coalesced
The size of the lesions ranged from approximately 2 to 3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
There was no hair growth at the site of the lesions
He was previously treated for tinea versicolor, without success
Histopathologic findings showed plate-like subepidermal tumor extending horizontally under epidermis with multiple cord-like connections to overlying epidermis
Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells with cytoplasm showing strong periodic acid-Schiff staining due to glycogen accumulation
Stroma formed by fibrous connective tissue
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor
Multiple round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Lesions ranged from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
Absence of hair growth in affected areas

concepts.why: The presence of hypopigmented macules, subepidermal tumor, and elastosis are consistent with Degos disease.
The histopathologic findings of neoplastic cords with clear/pale epithelial cells and strong periodic acid-Schiff staining are characteristic of Extramammary Paget disease.
The presence of multiple round, hypopigmented macules and the absence of hair growth are consistent with Syringoma.
The presence of hypopigmented macules and the absence of hair growth are consistent with Trichoepithelioma.
The histopathologic findings of a subepidermal tumor with multiple cord-like connections to overlying epidermis are characteristic of Basal cell carcinoma.
The presence of multiple round, hypopigmented macules is consistent with Seborrheic keratosis.
The presence of hypopigmented macules and the absence of hair growth are consistent with Dermatofibroma.
The histopathologic findings of neoplastic cords with clear/pale epithelial cells and strong periodic acid-Schiff staining are characteristic of Eccrine poroma.

rationales.F02: The presence of round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on the face and neck is more typical of Degos disease and Syringoma.
rationales.F05: The absence of hair growth at the site of the lesions is more typical of Degos disease and less typical of Syringoma and Trichoepithelioma.
rationales.F07: The histopathologic findings of a plate-like subepidermal tumor with multiple cord-like connections to the overlying epidermis are more typical of Extramammary Paget disease and Eccrine poroma.
rationales.F08: The presence of neoplastic cords with clear/pale epithelial cells and strong periodic acid-Schiff staining due to glycogen accumulation is more typical of Extramammary Paget disease and Eccrine poroma.

frontier_selector.rationale: Histopathologic findings of plate-like subepidermal tumor with cord-like connections and clear/pale epithelial cells showing strong periodic acid-Schiff staining due to glycogen accumulation support Eccrine poroma, with Extramammary Paget disease as a close runner-up due to similar histopathologic features
